p: He was shot five times. He fell among the boulders south of Big Round Top, a general for four days.

p: The charge accomplished nothing. No Confederate position was taken, no Union position was relieved. The men who survived came back to their starting line having given nothing and gained nothing.

p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 1 of 14

p: Colonize Silas Colgrove had received instructions to clear Confederate infantry from their position at the base of Culp's Hill. The 2nd Massachusetts and the 27th Indiana were to charge across an open meadow — perhaps 200 yards of ground fully exposed to Confederate fire from the woods beyond.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 2 of 14

p: Lieutenant Colonel Charles Mudge commanded the 2nd Massachusetts. He read the order and then read it again.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 3 of 14

p: He sent an aide back to Colgrove. Was the order correct? Had there been a mistake?

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 4 of 14

p: The aide came back. The order was confirmed.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 5 of 14

p: Mudge looked at the meadow. He looked at his regiment — 316 men who had served through two years of war, who had marched from Maryland to Pennsylvania, who trusted him.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 6 of 14

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 7 of 14

p: 'It is murder,' he said. 'But it is the order.'

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 8 of 14

p: He drew his saber and led the 2nd Massachusetts across the meadow at the double-quick.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 9 of 14

p: The Confederate fire from the woods was immediate and accurate. Men fell as they ran. Mudge was hit almost at once — shot through the throat, killed instantly, falling in the open ground he had called murder to cross.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 10 of 14

p: The regiment reached the Confederate position, could not hold it, and withdrew. In the few minutes of the charge and its aftermath, 136 of 316 men were casualties — 43 percent.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (narrative vignette)
p.short: Site vignette “Mudge and the Charge at Culp's Hill”, paragraph 11 of 14

p: The 27th Indiana charged alongside them. It did not go better.
